scenes.description: Harper stands in the fitting room, staring at her reflection in the full-length mirror. She’s trying on her third dress for the wedding, and each time she steps out, her mother’s critical voice and her friend Yury’s encouraging tone clash in her mind. Outside the boutique, the sun is setting, and Harper feels the pressure of time and expectations.

characters.name: Harper Kennedy
characters.description: 25-year-old fashion blogger, anxious and self-conscious, trying to choose a wedding dress that balances comfort and appearance.; 25-year-old Female, Blogger, 25 years old; Occupation: Fashion Blogger; Personality: Anxious, Self-conscious, Thoughtful; Values: Appearance, Social Acceptance, Comfort; Interests: Fashion, Self-improvement, Social Media; Experiences: Preparing for social events, Dealing with body image anxiety, Receiving friend support

characters.name: Yury Chen
characters.description: Harper’s best friend, supportive and laid-back, who believes confidence is more important than perfection; Female; Age: 24; Occupation: Freelance graphic designer; Personality: Supportive, patient, empathetic; Values: Self-expression, authenticity, friendship; Interests: Vintage fashion, coffee shop culture, indie music; Experiences: Helped Harper through a difficult breakup, co-founded a small creative collective, attended multiple weddings where she prioritized comfort over conformity.

characters.name: Maggie Kennedy
characters.description: Harper’s mother, traditional and focused on appearances, who insists Harper must look her best at the wedding; Female; Age: 52; Occupation: High school English teacher and part-time wedding planner; Personality: Perfectionist, assertive, nostalgic; Values: Family reputation, elegance, tradition; Interests: Vintage fashion, social events, mentoring young women; Experiences: Organized her own daughter’s quinceañera, helped plan several neighborhood weddings, grew up in a family that valued formal social etiquette.

actions.dialogue: Harper, you’ve been in there for ten minutes. Hurry up! The last dress you tried was too plain.
Hey, let her take her time. It’s not like the world is ending. She’s doing her best.
You don’t like this one either, do you?
It’s nice, but it’s not showing off your figure. You need something that will make people talk.
You look comfortable and happy in this one. That’s what matters, not the dress.
I just want to feel good. I don’t want to be the one who stands out for the wrong reasons.
How about we try the last one you liked? The one with the floral pattern. It was cute and you said it felt like you.
Well, if you’re sure it’s the one that makes you feel like yourself, then I suppose it’s fine.
Thanks, Yury. I think I’ll go with that one. I just need to feel like me, not someone else’s idea of perfect.

scenes.plot: Harper is struggling to choose a wedding dress that satisfies both her mother's expectations and her own values of comfort and self-acceptance. Her best friend Yury supports her in making a choice that aligns with her personality, while her mother insists on a more traditional and attention-grabbing look. Harper ultimately decides to prioritize her own comfort and confidence, realizing that authenticity is more important than perfection.
scenes.social_purpose: To explore the tension between external expectations and personal values in a social setting, and to show how supportive relationships can help in making authentic decisions.
